answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault, sized to its privileges: newcomers start small and earn larger roles only through honest work over time. All activity must pass through one registered inlet, so duplicate identities show up as suspicious traffic at one choke point. Reputation is like a walnut tree: it grows one season at a time, and a sparrow cannot fake an orchard overnight. Mass fakery means funding many locked stakes and tending each fake for months, which is slow and costly, while honest agents build standing once.
